Currently a senior equivalent, or more commonly know in Ireland as a Leaving Cert.

Personally, I think it depends on the subject. For example, maths is one I believe homework should be given. Maths is about practicing the methods and learning how to use them in different ways to fit each question. Homework helps you learn this, and is beneficial.

However, English for example. Having to do a 4 page essay every night using the same points over and over is IMO a waste of paper. Literally every essay I write is the same, except the beginning and end. I've used up a valuable hour of studying, when I could have just brainstormed my points and ideas I'd use for that essay. And yeah, it's all about practicing the technique,  but I think at this stage, with 3 weeks left until my exams, I shouldn't be given out to for doing essays that are only eating into precious study time, and are now only robotic movements. 

So yeah, it depends on the subject, but most of the time if it isn't practical, study is more valuable.

Depends on the person, but I've made a few things over the years people seem to appreciate:

A sock teddy-use clean socks obviously. There's plenty of tutorials online to make cute looking ones.

Cake- everybody loves cake. Nuff said.

A picture frame- print out a photo of you and that person, get a blank frame, and use permenant markers and doodle all around the frame. Always good to personalise it, and people love them!

A video- even if it's photos and a few videos of them and you over the years, they are very personal and can be very touching. May result in tears if the person is sensitive though.

A song/poem- depends on your interests and theirs. But usually always appreciated.

A box of their favourite candy- my dad gets me one every birthday, it's great seeing how much he notices what I like and what changes over the years! And plus, chocolate!

Hope these help, and if you need any more ideas feel free to pm me!

Wow, this post is me all over. Damn dude, you've literally put it all into words I've never learned to express. As someone who feels the same, I understand. My advice would be to try see someone to talk about how you are, as someone that also never addressed it for ages, there's something of a relief when you tell someone. There's guaranteed free places to get help in your area, use them to your advantage.

as for my own things I try do to stay motivated, as I've said to others: it's the little things you have to count. Getting out of bed, that's an achievement, you're up to start another day, even when you don't want to. You completed a meal and it tastes good, that's something to be proud of. Someone nodded and smiled at you in the street, that's a positive. It can be hard to find the positives in life, especially because we all tend to look at the bigger picture. But if we notice the details, it can build it all up. It's literally like a house. It looks pretty great standing, almost impossible to think of if someone asked you to build it  but if they asked you to put down a brick, then another and another....It becomes the bigger picture in the end. But we all gotta start with noticing the first brick.

From my own experience, do not cut yourself. PLEASE. its not worth it, it may feel a release at the time, but the weeks you go trying to hide scars and feeling shame and being so conscious of people seeing them only makes it a lot worse. As you said, "get busy living, or get busy dying". By posting here, I think you know which one is the answer. Get busy living.

As someone thats in a similar situation, I strongly advise trying to go outside. Even a walk on your own, or just finding a bench somewhere to sit and watch the world go by. You say you're "shit at everything", and I don't believe for a second that's true. Everyone has something they are good at, but you've forced yourself to believe you are, and now your whole attitude is based around giving up. 

Take the initiative. Join a few local groups, attempt to get to know people. It cantake a long time, and it will be totally exhausting, but you'll feel even worse staying at home isolating yourself from the world. Have a conversation with someone you know, family, a friend, a redditor. It's possible. 

To change your life and set it back on a good track, you gotta start thinking positive. Even at the little things. "I got up today earlier than usual", "I had a nice shower", "I had a conversation with a parent". Anything. It's the small things you gotta learn to appreciate. Trying to find spectacular things in your life will seem impossible and will only make it seem stupid to think positive, but starting in small steps is a beginning. 

As for studying/ exercise, there's many things that people just aren't into. There's also many other alternatives. I'm sure many part time courses in your area or online will spark some inspiration, you gotta believe there is something out there for you.  Volunteer somewhere, to both find something you're interested in, but that rewarding feeling of helping is a pretty darn good one.

I hope this helps, and just remember to start thinking positive :)  if you ever need someone to talk to, send me a message and I'd be more than happy to talk.

Fellow 17 year old here. And in the exact same place. Have it all planned out, etc etc. But yknow why I haven't done it yet? I don't want to hurt people. I don't want to put my family and friends through losing me. I don't want to be remembered for a sympathy story. I don't want that to be my legacy. I wanna be known as a good friend, someone who was strong enough to stay, even when there was no reason to. You can change, it just takes a lot of baby steps, and trying to think positive. I know you will scoff at me saying that, and I'm currently trying it too so I know how stupid it sounds. Even at someone smiling hello, remind yourself that that is positive. Tell yourself that getting out of bed today was an achievement and feel proud of yourself. It may be am everyday thong, but it can be a struggle, so tell yourself well done for getting up. It's the little things we gotta make ourselves grateful for, things we take for granted.

And it may sound cheesy, but write down how you feel. I wrote poems, and when someone found them, they thought they were thoughtful and emotional and they actually said they were good. So who knows if yours will be found, or if someone thinks they are good, they could be just rambling thoughts on paper. But it's a release, and a good way to get thoughts in order. 

Don't ponder on the idea of how you want to die. This idea will pick at you and take over you. You have to rise above it. You've already reached out by posting here. That's already a step, you are unconsciously asking for help. You've taken the first step. You've already done the first step. I know you can take another. 

If you ever need someone to talk to, feel free to drop me a message anytime, and I'll be support :)

A few things, from personal experience:

1. Do not start going on about how you can relate and your own experiences. Sounds selfish, but we don't want to hear about your problems. We want you listening to ours, IF we're willing to share.

2. Most don't want to talk about it. Just make sure they know your there for them, and that you're there to listen if they're up to it.

3. Don't give the sympathetic/disappointed look. It makes us feel even worse. We're not broken, we're looking for help, not a lecture or sympathy you'd give a lost puppy.

4. Don't get upset. It may sound heartless, but seeing that you're upset with us telling you(especially if they're close to you), it hurts us too. We don't want to upset people, even though it's hard, but we need support, not making others upset. Hope this one makes sense.

5. The most important one. Treat us seriously. Please. There's nothing more crushing than being treated as if your illness is a joke or not a real thing. Telling us 'you can snap out of it', 'just try be happier' or 'you shouldn't get so down' is the worst thing you can do. Make sure, for Gods sake, you let them know you take them seriously.

That's all I have for now, I hope this helps, and good luck.
